complexity_rationale: Idempotent webhook with strict (paymentIntentId, providerStatus) dedup keyed on sha256(intentId||providerStatus) per ADR-006; payment-intent state machine REQUIRES_PAYMENT -> {SUCCEEDED|FAILED|EXPIRED} guarded by amount-FIRST check (PAY-006) and terminal-state guard; outbox event production on the dedup-cleared path; in-process expiry sweeper (60s tick, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) that NEVER emits events; producer of two domain events (payment.completed, payment.failed) with strict per-orderId ordering. Producer-only — Order and Inventory consume; Payment NEVER calls Order or Inventory directly. Callback authentication = HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, MOCK_PROVIDER_SECRET) with constant-time compare + timestamp anti-replay. Internal callers authenticate via X-Internal-Secret per ADR-008 (INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET, crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare).
skills_invoked: crafting-backend-code (pattern-first scaffold for handler + outbox + dedup + sweeper)

produces_events: events.payment.expired (CONTRACT REFERENCED but NOT EMITTED in MVP — see expired_event_decision)
consumes_events_explicit_non_consumption: events.reservation.expired — Payment INTENTIONALLY does NOT consume this (ADR-009 + TL PR-001 LOCKED). The reservation sweeper drives PAYMENT_EXPIRED on Order/Inventory side; late callbacks for an expired intent return 409 PAYMENT_INTENT_TERMINAL.

events.order.cancelled — Payment is a CONSUMER per contract events.order.cancelled.consumers but the MVP transition is no-op for terminal intents and an in-tx flip (REQUIRES_PAYMENT -> CANCELLED) is documented; left for future iteration if a cancel-during-payment race surfaces. NOT in scope for v0.1 because the simulate flow is sync-fast enough to never observe the race.
upstream_sync_callers: checkout.commit -> payment.intent.create (X-Internal-Secret + Idempotency-Key=orderId, sync HTTP, step 8 of checkout 9-step orchestration)
frontend-web -> payment.simulate (customer JWT, role=CUSTOMER; ownership check on intent.owner_user_id)
mock-provider (or simulate's internal hop) -> payment.callback (HMAC-SHA256 webhook signature)

expired_event_decision.decision: DO NOT EMIT events.payment.expired in MVP
expired_event_decision.rationale: ADR-009 + TL PR-001 (LOCKED): the Inventory reservation sweeper publishes events.reservation.expired which Order consumes to transition PENDING_PAYMENT -> PAYMENT_EXPIRED, and Inventory consumes to release the reservation. Emitting events.payment.expired in addition would create duplicate-cancel cascades and double-handling on consumers. Payment's intent itself still ages out via this service's internal expiry_sweeper (see internal_handlers.expiry_sweeper) so that subsequent late callbacks 409 cleanly with PAYMENT_INTENT_TERMINAL. The producer contract events.payment.expired remains DEFINED in cross-cutting contracts (Order/Inventory keep state-driven consumers for it as a future safety net), but Payment's outbox writer simply does not emit it for any path in MVP.
expired_event_decision.future_enablement_path: If a future provider integration distinguishes provider-driven 'EXPIRED' callbacks from sweeper-driven expiry, the dedup-cleared callback path with providerStatus=EXPIRED can begin emitting events.payment.expired. The handler scaffold reserves the branch (see internal_handlers.process_callback.outbox_emit_rules.EXPIRED) — guarded by feature flag PAYMENT_EMIT_EXPIRED_EVENT (default false in MVP).

endpoints.name: intent.create
endpoints.auth_detail: X-Internal-Secret header validated via common/middleware/internal_auth.go (per ADR-008): subtle.ConstantTimeCompare against INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET (or comma-separated rotation overlap value); reject 401 AUTH_INVALID on miss/wrong; NEVER log the supplied or expected secret value. Plain == / != string compare is FORBIDDEN.
endpoints.purpose: Create the payment intent for a freshly-created order. Idempotent on order_id per ADR + cross-cutting.idempotency.internal_orderId_rule. Caches intent.owner_user_id from request body (forwarded from checkout's identity.profile.read) so payment.simulate ownership check needs no sync hop to identity/order.

ownerUserId.description: Cached from Checkout's identity.profile.read; pinned at create time so payment.simulate ownership check is a local row read.

expiresAt.description: Optional; defaults to created_at + 15min (matches reservation TTL)

request_headers.Idempotency-Key: <orderId UUID v7> (REQUIRED — cross-cutting.idempotency.internal_orderId_rule; handler validates header == request.orderId else 400 VALIDATION_ERROR)

validation_rules: orderId is a valid UUID v7 (common/validator)
amount > 0 and within int64 range (common/validator gt=0)
If a payment_intents row already exists for orderId AND status=REQUIRES_PAYMENT -> return 200 with the existing intent (idempotent replay)
If a payment_intents row already exists for orderId AND status TERMINAL (SUCCEEDED|FAILED|EXPIRED) -> 409 CONFLICT { reason: 'intent already TERMINAL for orderId' }

error_contract.trigger: any field violates schema OR Idempotency-Key != orderId
intent already exists for orderId in TERMINAL state

edge_behavior.idempotency: Idempotent on order_id (UNIQUE constraint backs it). Same orderId returns existing intent. Different request body (e.g. mismatched amount) for an existing REQUIRES_PAYMENT intent -> return existing record verbatim — body mismatch is NOT honored because amount is server-derived from order.total at the Checkout layer. TTL: row lives until terminal-state retention (>= 30 days; cleanup is future-iteration concern).
side_effects: INSERT payment_intents row in single tx; no event emitted at create time
edge_behavior.transactionality: single-row INSERT; on UNIQUE violation re-SELECT and return cached payload

implementation_hints: Use common/middleware/internal_auth.go for X-Internal-Secret
Use common/database pgx pool for INSERT
Use common/wrapper.Respond for the {code,message,data,traceId} envelope
Use common/generator (UUID v7) for intent_id
Use common/validator struct tags for schema validation

endpoints.name: intent.simulate
endpoints.auth_detail: JWT ES256 via common/middleware.JWT; role=CUSTOMER required (else 403 AUTH_FORBIDDEN). After token validation, the handler MUST verify claims.sub == payment_intents.owner_user_id (the cached owner from intent.create); mismatch is 403 AUTH_FORBIDDEN with message 'forbidden' (NEVER 'not your order' — do not leak ownership to the caller).
callers: frontend-web (the customer's mock 'pick a scenario' screen on the payment route)
endpoints.purpose: Customer-facing mock: translate outcome (success|failed|timeout) to providerStatus (SUCCEEDED|FAILED|EXPIRED), generate a deterministic mock_provider_ref, then INVOKE process_callback() in-process (same canonical idempotent path as the webhook). Does NOT directly write payment_intents.status — every transition goes through process_callback.
validation_rules: paymentIntentId resolves to a payment_intents row else PAYMENT_INTENT_NOT_FOUND
Map outcome -> providerStatus: success->SUCCEEDED, failed->FAILED, timeout->EXPIRED

error_contract.trigger: outcome not in enum or paymentIntentId not a UUID
intent already in SUCCEEDED|FAILED|EXPIRED and outcome differs (delegated to process_callback Step 5 terminal-state guard)

edge_behavior.idempotency: First simulate wins. Subsequent simulate with the SAME outcome on a TERMINAL intent -> 200 with replay envelope (process_callback Step 4 returns the cached envelope). Subsequent simulate with a DIFFERENT outcome on a TERMINAL intent -> 409 PAYMENT_INTENT_TERMINAL via Step 5.
side_effects: Inline call into process_callback() which (on dedup-clear) UPDATEs payment_intents row, INSERTs payment_callback_dedup row, INSERTs payment.outbox_events row in same tx
edge_behavior.transactionality: delegates to process_callback's single tx (FOR UPDATE on intent + tx-write outbox)

implementation_hints: Generate mock_provider_ref = 'MOCKPAY-' + base32(sha256(intent_id || outcome))[:10] — deterministic so re-simulate yields same ref; common/hash exposes sha256
Set provider_timestamp = clock.Now() (common/clock for testability)
Call into internal_handlers.process_callback in the same goroutine; do NOT cross HTTP boundary
Use common/middleware.JWT then a tiny per-handler ownership-check middleware that reads the intent and compares claims.sub to owner_user_id

endpoints.name: intent.callback
endpoints.auth_detail: Webhook signature: header X-Mock-Provider-Signature = hex(HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, MOCK_PROVIDER_SECRET)). Validation algorithm: (1) verify X-Mock-Provider-Timestamp header is RFC3339 and within +/-5min skew (replay window); (2) compute expected = hmac.New(sha256, MOCK_PROVIDER_SECRET).Write(rawBody).Sum(nil); (3) hex-decode supplied signature; (4) compare via crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare (NEVER plain == / !=); (5) reject 401 AUTH_INVALID on any failure; NEVER log the body, signature, or secret. Algorithm SHA256 is pinned in code (no caller-controlled algo selection — defends CVE-2018-1000613 class). MOCK_PROVIDER_SECRET MIN length 32 bytes validated at startup.
callers: mock provider (real or simulated). In MVP, simulate also goes through process_callback() in-process and skips this HTTP hop entirely.
endpoints.purpose: The dedup + idempotency entry point. Validates HMAC signature + timestamp skew, validates body, then calls internal_handlers.process_callback() — the canonical 7-step ordering.
validation_rules: X-Mock-Provider-Signature header present and HMAC-SHA256 verifies via crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare against expected over the RAW body bytes (NOT re-marshaled JSON)
X-Mock-Provider-Timestamp header present, parses as RFC3339, and is within +/-5min of now (replay protection)
paymentIntentId resolves to a payment_intents row else PAYMENT_INTENT_NOT_FOUND
amount equals payment_intents.amount_minor (PAY-006 PRECEDES dedup_key derivation — see process_callback Step 1 ordering)

error_contract.trigger: schema violation (missing field, bad enum, malformed UUID)
missing/bad signature OR timestamp out of skew window OR missing/wrong INTERNAL guard if reused
callback.amount != intent.amount_minor (PAY-006); intent stays REQUIRES_PAYMENT, no dedup row, no outbox
intent already TERMINAL AND incoming providerStatus differs from the original

edge_behavior.idempotency: STRICT idempotency on (paymentIntentId, providerStatus). Dedup key = sha256(intent_id || '|' || provider_status). Replay returns the cached envelope; NEVER re-fires outbox event. Different providerStatus against a TERMINAL intent -> 409 PAYMENT_INTENT_TERMINAL.
edge_behavior.dedup_window: 30 days (matches cross-cutting.idempotency floor for payment.callback; matches provider redelivery horizon).
side_effects: Single tx: lock intent FOR UPDATE -> amount-check -> dedup-key compute -> replay return OR terminal-state guard OR transition (UPDATE intent + INSERT outbox row + INSERT dedup row, all same tx)
edge_behavior.transactionality: Single Postgres tx in process_callback. FOR UPDATE on payment_intents + UNIQUE on dedup_key are joint defenses against concurrent callbacks.

implementation_hints: Bind raw body via gin's c.GetRawData() BEFORE c.ShouldBindJSON; HMAC must hash exactly the bytes the provider signed
Use common/middleware/webhook_signature.go (NEW shared helper, pattern-mirrors common/middleware/internal_auth.go) for HMAC verify + timestamp skew
Use crypto/hmac + crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare directly; NO third-party HMAC libs
Use common/database tx wrapper for the single-tx process_callback path
Use common/kafka producer (NOT in handler — outbox publisher is a separate goroutine; see internal_handlers.outbox_relay)

internal_handlers.name: process_callback
internal_handlers.purpose: SINGLE canonical function invoked by both the HTTP webhook and payment.simulate. Owns the dedup + state-machine transition + outbox-write inside ONE Postgres transaction. The 7-step ordering is the load-bearing security contract.

inputs.intent_id: UUID (server-validated; from URL/lookup, NEVER directly from caller body alone for dedup-key derivation)
inputs.mock_provider_ref: string (max 64; persisted but NOT in dedup_key)
inputs.amount_from_caller: BIGINT minor (UNTRUSTED — used ONLY for amount-mismatch validation against payment_intents.amount_minor)

canonical_7_step_ordering: 1. LOCK intent: SELECT * FROM payment_intents WHERE intent_id=:intent_id FOR UPDATE

2. AMOUNT-CHECK (BEFORE terminal-state guard): IF amount_from_caller != intent.amount_minor THEN ROLLBACK + RETURN 409 PAYMENT_AMOUNT_MISMATCH. Critical ordering — placing amount-check BEFORE the terminal-state guard means an attacker cannot bypass amount validation by replaying an old (paymentIntentId, providerStatus) pair on a terminal intent with a tweaked amount. Without this ordering, the terminal-state path could write a dedup row keyed on the contradicting status, masking the amount tampering.

3. DEDUP-KEY DERIVE: dedup_key := sha256(intent.intent_id::text || '|' || provider_status). Server-recorded fields ONLY. NO user-controlled body fields (mockPaymentRef, amount, providerTimestamp) participate.

4. REPLAY RETURN CACHED ENVELOPE: existing := SELECT * FROM payment_callback_dedup WHERE dedup_key=:dedup_key. IF existing IS NOT NULL THEN COMMIT (no writes) + RETURN existing.envelope WITH existing.http_status. NEVER re-fires outbox.

5. TERMINAL-STATE GUARD: IF intent.status IN (SUCCEEDED|FAILED|EXPIRED) THEN build envelope=409 PAYMENT_INTENT_TERMINAL { currentStatus, attemptedStatus }, INSERT dedup row keyed on the (intent_id, provider_status) pair so future replays of THIS terminal-conflict get the same cached envelope, COMMIT, RETURN envelope. Reaching here means: same intent already TERMINAL AND incoming status DIFFERS from original.

6. TRANSITION + OUTBOX in SAME TX: new_status := MAP provider_status (SUCCEEDED->SUCCEEDED, FAILED->FAILED, EXPIRED->EXPIRED). UPDATE payment_intents SET status=new_status, mock_provider_ref=:ref, provider_status=:provider_status, paid_at=(SUCCEEDED ? :provider_timestamp : NULL), updated_at=now(), version=version+1 WHERE intent_id=:intent_id AND version=intent.version. Then emit_outbox_event(intent, new_status) — INSERT one row into payment.outbox_events for SUCCEEDED|FAILED only; EXPIRED is skipped in MVP per expired_event_decision.

7. DEDUP-SUCCESS ROW: INSERT INTO payment_callback_dedup (dedup_key, intent_id, provider_status, envelope=success_envelope, http_status=200, expires_at=now()+30d). ON CONFLICT (dedup_key) DO NOTHING — defense-in-depth against a concurrent racer that beat us past Step 4 but lost the FOR UPDATE; in that case the racer's envelope is canonical. Then COMMIT; log structured {dedup_key, intent_id, action='APPLIED'}; RETURN envelope.
ordering_rationale: FOR UPDATE before everything serializes concurrent callbacks for the same intent — race losers wait at Step 1 and find the world post-mutation when they run.

AMOUNT-CHECK before TERMINAL guard so an attacker cannot bypass amount validation by replaying a (intentId, providerStatus) pair on a terminal intent with a tweaked amount; without this ordering, terminal-state path writes a dedup row that masks the amount tampering.
DEDUP-KEY composed from server-trusted fields ONLY; if mockPaymentRef or amount were in the key, an attacker could force dedup misses by changing those fields.
REPLAY RETURN before TERMINAL guard so a same-status replay gets the cached SUCCESS envelope, not a misleading 409 TERMINAL.
TRANSITION + OUTBOX in SAME tx is the outbox-pattern guarantee (ADR-004): no phantom event without state change, no missing event with state change.
DEDUP-SUCCESS row written INSIDE the same tx so a crash between transition and dedup write rolls back BOTH; on retry the same callback re-runs cleanly through Step 4.

outbox_emit_rules.SUCCEEDED: INSERT outbox_events (id=uuidv7(), event_id=uuidv7(), aggregate_type='payment_intent', aggregate_id=intent_id, event_type='payment.completed', topic='ecom.payment.events', partition_key=intent.order_id, payload={eventId, occurredAt:now(), orderId:intent.order_id, paymentIntentId:intent.intent_id, amount:intent.amount_minor, mockPaymentRef:input.mock_provider_ref}, status='PENDING')
outbox_emit_rules.FAILED: INSERT outbox_events (... event_type='payment.failed', payload={eventId, occurredAt, orderId, paymentIntentId, reason:'PROVIDER_DECLINED'}, status='PENDING')
outbox_emit_rules.EXPIRED: DO NOT INSERT outbox row in MVP (see expired_event_decision). Feature flag PAYMENT_EMIT_EXPIRED_EVENT default false; the branch exists in code but is gated.

internal_handlers.concurrency_notes: FOR UPDATE on payment_intents.intent_id serializes concurrent callbacks for one intent. Two callbacks with the SAME provider_status race -> loser hits Step 4 (REPLAY RETURN) on the next pass. Two callbacks with DIFFERENT provider_status race -> loser hits Step 5 (PAYMENT_INTENT_TERMINAL). The UNIQUE PRIMARY KEY on payment_callback_dedup is defense-in-depth for any cross-replica racer that bypasses the row lock (e.g., split-brain).
logging_redaction: ALWAYS log: dedup_key (the sha256 hash, NOT the inputs), intent_id, order_id, action (APPLIED|REPLAY_HIT|TERMINAL|AMOUNT_MISMATCH), traceId, durationMs.

NEVER log: the callback request body or any subset of it (mockPaymentRef, providerTimestamp, amount, paymentIntentId-from-body), the X-Mock-Provider-Signature header value, the MOCK_PROVIDER_SECRET, the FULL contents of the dedup envelope (only its http_status + code), provider PII fields if any (future-provider safety).

internal_handlers.name: expiry_sweeper
internal_handlers.purpose: In-process periodic job that flips REQUIRES_PAYMENT intents past expires_at to status=EXPIRED so any subsequent late callback returns PAYMENT_INTENT_TERMINAL cleanly via process_callback Step 5. INTERNAL-ONLY — emits NO outbox event (the Inventory reservation sweeper drives Order/Inventory via events.reservation.expired per ADR-009 + TL PR-001).
internal_handlers.schedule: Every 60 seconds (env PAYMENT_EXPIRY_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SEC, default 60). In-process goroutine started at boot in main.go.
internal_handlers.scan_query: SELECT intent_id, version FROM payment_intents WHERE status='REQUIRES_PAYMENT' AND expires_at < now() ORDER BY expires_at LIMIT :batch_size FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
internal_handlers.transition: Per row in its own short tx: UPDATE payment_intents SET status='EXPIRED', updated_at=now(), version=version+1 WHERE intent_id=? AND status='REQUIRES_PAYMENT' AND version=:version. NO outbox write. NO dedup-row write (the dedup table is for callback replays only). Use SKIP LOCKED so multiple replicas of the payment service can run the sweeper concurrently without serializing on a single advisory lock.
metrics: counter payment_expiry_sweeper_flipped_total — number of intents flipped REQUIRES_PAYMENT -> EXPIRED
gauge payment_expiry_sweeper_lag_seconds — max(now() - expires_at) for any still-REQUIRES_PAYMENT past-expiry intent (alarms if lag > 90s)
internal_handlers.rationale: Without this sweeper, a late provider callback could arrive at an unaged REQUIRES_PAYMENT intent, transition it to SUCCEEDED, and emit events.payment.completed. But Order has already moved to PAYMENT_EXPIRED via the reservation sweeper path, so Order's state-driven consumer (ADR-009) would log the late event and ignore it. Functionally correct but operationally opaque — running this sweeper makes Payment's own state honest and produces a clean 409 PAYMENT_INTENT_TERMINAL response for the provider's late retry instead of a misleading 200.
implementation_hints: Pattern-mirror inventory's reservation-sweeper (already documented in inventory td.json)
Use common/database pgx pool with explicit tx
Use FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so two pods don't fight over the same row
Panic-recovery wrapper around the loop body so one bad row doesn't kill the goroutine

internal_handlers.name: outbox_relay
internal_handlers.purpose: Single-threaded goroutine per payment service replica that drains payment.outbox_events to Kafka topic ecom.payment.events with partition_key = order_id. ADR-004 outbox pattern.
internal_handlers.schedule: Every 5s OR when notified via channel by the writer (LISTEN/NOTIFY optional v2 optimization).
internal_handlers.scan_query: SELECT id, aggregate_id, event_id, event_type, topic, partition_key, payload FROM payment.outbox_events WHERE published_at IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 100
internal_handlers.publish: common/kafka producer.Send(topic, key=partition_key, value=payload). On success: UPDATE payment.outbox_events SET published_at=now() WHERE id=:id. On failure: increment attempts; backoff; max 10 attempts then mark status=FAILED + alert (counter payment_outbox_failed_total, gauge payment_outbox_pending_count).
internal_handlers.ordering_guarantee: Per-aggregate (per-orderId) order preserved by ORDER BY id (UUID v7 ~= time-ordered) + partition_key=order_id mapping. NO global ordering across orderIds — that's intentional per ADR-009.
implementation_hints: Use common/kafka producer + producer_interceptor (already in common)
Single goroutine per replica; if multi-replica throughput becomes an issue, partition the outbox by id hash (deferred)
Idempotent at consumer side via consumed_events(eventId PK) — see contract events.payment.completed.idempotency_rules

test_strategy.unit: table-driven tests per handler with pgxmock or testcontainers Postgres; mock common/kafka producer; mock clock via common/clock; assert log redaction by intercepting slog handler.
test_strategy.integration: docker-compose up payment + Kafka + Postgres; curl smoke through intent.create -> simulate(success) -> assert outbox row -> drain to Kafka -> assert event arrives. Replay smoke: post identical callback twice -> assert one outbox row, second response = first envelope verbatim.

ba_acceptance_mapping.ba_ref: PAY-007 — payment_intents persists mock_provider_ref, provider_status, paid_at
PAY-004 + ORD-009 — Order's PAYMENT_EXPIRED is driven by Inventory's events.reservation.expired sweeper, NOT by Payment emitting events.payment.expired
PAY-002 + PAY-006 — exact match transitions PAID

security_posture_for_reviewer_l1: Webhook signature: HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, MOCK_PROVIDER_SECRET); algo PINNED in code (no caller-controlled selection); secret per-env via config; constant-time compare via crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare; body MUST be the raw bytes (not parsed JSON re-serialized).
Replay protection: X-Mock-Provider-Timestamp header REQUIRED, parsed RFC3339, compared against now() with +/-5min skew tolerance; reject 401 outside the window.

Internal-secret auth (intent.create): X-Internal-Secret validated via crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare per ADR-008; INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET env-var name LOCKED; MIN 32 bytes; comma-separated rotation supported. Plain == / != comparison is a high-severity reviewer finding.
Idempotency-Key on intent.create MUST equal request.orderId (cross-cutting.idempotency.internal_orderId_rule); else 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

Dedup key composition: server-recorded fields ONLY (intent_id from validated lookup + provider_status from validated enum). NO user-controlled body fields (mockPaymentRef, amount, providerTimestamp) in the key.

Amount-mismatch check runs BEFORE the terminal-state guard (process_callback Step 2 vs Step 5) — attacker cannot bypass amount validation by replaying a (paymentIntentId, providerStatus) pair on a terminal intent with a tweaked amount; without this ordering, the terminal-path dedup row would mask the amount tampering.
Outbox writes happen in the SAME tx as the intent state transition (process_callback Step 6). ADR-004 outbox pattern.

Logging redaction: log {dedup_key, intent_id, order_id, action, traceId} only; NEVER log the callback request body, signature header value, MOCK_PROVIDER_SECRET, INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET, or the FULL dedup envelope (only its http_status + code).

Auth boundaries: intent.create = X-Internal-Secret only (internal); intent.simulate = customer JWT + ownership check on intent.owner_user_id (claim-against-row, NOT the request body); intent.callback = HMAC signature + timestamp skew. None of the three boundaries trust the request body for authorization.

Late-callback handling: terminal-state guard returns 409 with a dedup row written so future replays of the conflict get the same envelope (no oscillation between TERMINAL and AMOUNT_MISMATCH on a re-tweaked retry).

ownership-check (simulate) compares claims.sub to payment_intents.owner_user_id WITHOUT leaking ownership in the error message; AUTH_FORBIDDEN message stays generic ('forbidden'), not 'not your order'.
ownership-check uses the cached owner_user_id on payment_intents (set at intent.create time) — NO sync hop to identity or order on the simulate hot path.
qa_l1_test_matrix_anchor: see test_strategy.happy_paths + test_strategy.negative_paths above; all 22 cases are required acceptance criteria.

Future enablement of events.payment.expired emission gated by feature flag PAYMENT_EMIT_EXPIRED_EVENT (see expired_event_decision.future_enablement_path).

events.order.cancelled (declared consumer per contract; MVP scope is no-op-on-terminal)
